rationale: This conceptual and methodological paper offers research proposals and methodological notes on investigating how water access affects subjective well-being (happiness). It presents no empirical primary data or systematic synthesis (E05), reverses the causal direction of interest (treating water access as a predictor of subjective well-being rather than an access outcome), and does not empirically examine any legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism governing service access beyond noting potential relevance to human-rights framing and NGO/government decision-making.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2: the paper is a conceptual/methodological proposal to study how water access affects subjective well-being rather than an empirical evaluation of any legal, administrative, institutional, or governance determinant of water access.

evidence_quotes.quote: In this paper we offer several proposals in order to investigate the relationship between water access and happiness, suggesting some situations that would merit further research.
Moreover, we have included some methodological notes in order to achieve this objective.

Firstly, it can favour the contemplation of water access as a human right. Secondly, it can serve as a framework for the decision-making process carried out by Governments and NGOs in developing countries.
